title: Pumas Stun Tigres 5-0 to Reach First-Ever Liga MX Femenil Semifinal as América, Chivas and Rayadas Advance — Semis Set for Dec. 9-13
excerpt: Pumas pulled off the biggest upset in years, routing Tigres 5-0 at El Volcán to win 7-3 on aggregate and reach the semifinals for the first time, where they will face América in the Clásico Capitalino while Chivas meet Monterrey.
content:
MONTERREY — Pumas delivered the biggest upset in years in the Liga MX Femenil playoffs, routing Tigres 5-0 in the second leg at Estadio Universitario on Saturday to win the quarterfinal 7-3 on aggregate and reach the semifinals for the first time in club history.

Stephanie Ribeiro scored twice, and Priscila Chinchilla, Montserrat Hernández and Elena Sainz added goals in the historic rout at El Volcán. Tigres had won the first leg 3-2 at Estadio Olímpico Universitario, so Pumas needed to win by two goals to advance — they won by five.

Defending champions América cruised through as well, beating Toluca 3-0 in the second leg to complete a 6-0 aggregate win. Geyse, Priscila and Scarlett Camberos scored the goals that sealed the series, after América had won the first leg 3-0 at Estadio Banorte on an own goal by Mitsy Ramírez, a header from Jana Gutiérrez and a penalty from Irene Guerrero.

Monterrey also advanced with a comeback, rallying from 2-0 down at halftime to beat Pachuca 3-2 in the second leg and 4-2 on aggregate, with goals from Valeria Del Campo, Diana García and Alexandra Godínez. Guadalajara drew 1-1 with FC Juárez in the second leg, advancing on a 1-1 aggregate thanks to a better regular-season finish after Alicia Cervantes equalized Farlyn Caicedo's opener.

The semifinals are set: Pumas face América in the Clásico Capitalino, and Chivas meet the Rayadas of Monterrey. The first legs are scheduled for Dec. 9-10, with the second legs Dec. 12-13, and América will close the series at home.

América head coach Ángel Villacampa confirmed the team will play its home semifinal — and a possible final — at Estadio Azteca, now known as Estadio Banorte. 'We will play at the Azteca, in our house, and it will not be any other way,' he said, adding that preparation is complicated by the FIFA break, with many América players away on national-team duty.

The playoffs now pause for three weeks for the Concacaf W Championship, where Mexico plays this weekend for qualification to the 2027 Women's World Cup and the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. The regular season ended with América and Rayadas as group leaders, both with 37 points.

Sources: MNI Noticias, Nov. 19, 2026; Claro Sports, Nov. 24, 2026; Lado.mx, Nov. 24, 2026; Sportradar, Nov. 24, 2026; Interact Post News, Nov. 25, 2026.
